correctness.rationale: Leibniz determines D from f=D(t), and f descends precisely when nt^{n−1}f vanishes: automatic at even n and exactly f∈(t) for odd n. At odd n one differentiates polynomial representatives and multiplies by f; the bare derivative alone need not descend. Since squaring a derivation in characteristic two gives a derivation, D² is zero iff ff′=0. With x=t² and R=k[x]/(x^s), write f=E+tH at even n and f=xE+tH at odd n, with the two parities disjoint and each summand represented by R. Then f′=H, and the even and odd coefficient blocks of ff′ vanish independently exactly for EH=0 and H²=0 in R. To check the rank independently, restrict D to the odd input block tR (it kills the even block). On odd inputs the output coefficient pair is (Eu,Hu) for u∈R, in the appropriate two parity summands. If v=min(v_x(E),v_x(H)), the kernel in R is x^{s−v}R, hence the rank is s−v in both dimensions. The zero pair agrees with v=s. For v≥ceil(s/2) there are q^{2(s−v)}−q^{2(s−v−1)} pairs at that minimum valuation. For v below that cutoff, H cannot attain v and must lie in x^{s−v}R, giving (q−1)q^{s−v−1}·q^v pairs. Independently, H=0 gives q^s solutions, and each nonzero valuation j of H with ceil(s/2)≤j≤s−1 gives (q−1)q^{s−j−1} choices of H and q^j choices of E. This checks the total, including s=1. The independent matrix replay checked all admissible D(t), testing the square on each basis column and performing field elimination for ranks: q=2, n=2,…,8 and q=4, n=2,…,6. It matched every claimed histogram, including both n=6 and n=7 over F₂. The proof establishes the full parameters and the explicit parity correspondence.
residual_risks: The matrix replay is finite. The all-length argument concerns composition-square zero and the linear rank on the whole algebra, not general nilpotency, conjugacy classes or unreduced scheme structures.
